title: Linked List Cycle
description:
Given the head of a linked list, return `true` if the list contains a cycle (some node can be reached again by following `next` pointers), otherwise `false`.

In the test inputs, `index` is only how the list is built: the position that the tail connects back to, or `-1` for no cycle. Your function receives just `head`. Try to use O(1) extra memory.

examples.explanation: The tail links back to the node with value 2.

constraints: 0 <= list length <= 1000 (stress tests go much longer)
index is -1 or a valid position
hints: Storing every visited node works, but costs O(n) memory. Can two pointers detect a loop without storing anything?
If one pointer moves faster than another inside a loop, what must eventually happen to the gap between them?
Move slow by 1 and fast by 2. If fast reaches None, there is no cycle. If slow and fast ever point to the same node, there is one.

solution.explanation: Use Floyd's tortoise and hare. Slow advances one node per step, fast advances two. Without a cycle, fast falls off the end and we return false. With a cycle, both enter the loop and fast gains one node on slow each step, so they must meet. That takes O(n) time and only two pointers of memory, O(1) space.
